text: A simple way to understand payment issues
I built a prototype that brings payment records, operational analytics, and evidence-based investigation into one workflow.

Opening: PayBridge is my payment-operations prototype. It helps an operator move from payment records to evidence and a recorded human decision. The project uses synthetic data and some illustrative incident content; it is not a live bank-routing system. Sources: README.md; backend/app/api/main.py; backend/app/agent/workflow.py.

title: The problem: payment issues take context to explain

text: The problem: payment issues take context to explain
A merchant sees a payment fail. The team needs to answer three things quickly:
Find the saved transaction and its status, method, source, and any recorded reason.
Compare outcomes across a group, such as UPI attempts by bank or gateway.
Gather evidence, review a recommendation, and record who made the decision.
PayBridge connects these steps in one prototype workflow.
It supports investigation and operational review; it does not guarantee a cause or fix.

Explain the real operational question: not just whether a payment failed, but whether many failures share a pattern and what evidence supports a response. A signal is not proof of fraud or provider fault. Sources: README.md; backend/app/services/payment_queries.py; backend/app/analytics/payment_analytics.py.

The repository’s runtime database and deployment storage must be checked for each environment.

Describe the architecture simply. Streamlit is the interface; FastAPI provides the service layer; SQL stores operational records; analytics and the AI workflow consume that evidence. SQLite is the configured default and PostgreSQL is supported by configuration, but don’t claim a production migration without verifying the deployed database. Sources: frontend/dashboard.py; backend/app/api/main.py; backend/app/core/config.py; backend/app/agent/workflow.py.

title: CSV import: validate first, then store accepted rows

text: CSV import: validate first, then store accepted rows
Write accepted rows and run history
See counts, rejected rows, and ledger data
This structures supported payment CSVs. It does not turn arbitrary files into verified payments or connect automatically to every provider.

Explain that ingestion is not magic parsing. The service maps recognized columns, normalizes fields, validates key values, deduplicates, saves accepted payment rows, and keeps an import run and rejection details. Only compatible CSVs are accepted; unrelated/unstructured files are not converted into trustworthy transactions. Sources: backend/app/services/ingestion_payments.py; backend/app/api/main.py.

title: Analytics counts outcomes; anomalies flag unusual patterns

text: Analytics counts outcomes; anomalies flag unusual patterns

Counts by status
Captured value (GMV)
Success rate from captured + failed outcomes

Groups outcomes by method, bank, or gateway
Applies minimum-volume and failure-rate rules
Creates a review target, not a fraud verdict
Pending and authorized payments are excluded from this denominator.

Give the simple math example: 80 captured and 20 failed gives 80/(80+20)=80% success. Pending/authorized are excluded. Captured GMV is transaction volume, not profit. Anomaly detection groups payments and applies rules; the repository’s threshold examples require a minimum attempt count. Do not state that every successful customer payment causes an anomaly. Sources: backend/app/analytics/payment_analytics.py; backend/app/ml/anomaly.py.

title: AI investigation combines facts, patterns, and procedures

text: AI investigation combines facts, patterns, and procedures

Saved transaction records
Status, method, bank, gateway, errors

SQL queries and metrics
Counts, rates, and group comparisons

RAG retrieves local procedure text
Text is context, not transaction truth
A human reviews the result. Unknown causes should stay unknown.

Explain RAG in one line: split local procedure documents into sections, retrieve relevant sections for a question, and pass them as context. SQL and metrics supply transaction evidence; RAG does not determine payment status. The code uses a local TF-IDF/cosine retrieval path by default, with optional Ollama support; do not claim a verified cloud LLM or LlamaIndex use for this repository. Some incident UI content remains hardcoded. Sources: backend/app/agent/workflow.py; backend/app/rag/store.py; backend/app/rag/ollama_client.py; frontend/views/ai_investigation_workspace.py.
It records a human decision and audit activity.
It does not make failed payments succeed or reroute live bank traffic.
This is the human-oversight step in the prototype.

Use this real example: a merchant reports a UPI failure spike; PayBridge assembles evidence and suggests a temporary routing response; an admin reviews and approves or rejects it; the decision is recorded. In this repository the action is local/simulated and does not change provider routing. Sources: backend/app/api/main.py; backend/app/agent/workflow.py; backend/app/models/ops.py.
